figures.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Create an original friendly hand-drawn technical explainer for a plain-language code walkthrough. Landscape target 1920x1080. White paper, slightly irregular navy pen outlines, blue and indigo marker headings, soft light-blue and lavender washes, recognizable documents/funnel/notebook/reviewer objects, plenty of white space. Avoid a generic block diagram, dense paragraphs, tiny labels, or copying old architectural claims. All essential text should remain readable at 850px display width.
Title exactly: "Building the taxonomy"
Purpose: show how the IMPLEMENTED GitHub Manager prepares taxonomy-discovery inputs and asks an LLM for a draft; do not imply RAKE alone creates taxonomy or that TF-IDF is used for discovery.
Arrange a clear numbered reading journey with generous spacing, using 5 semantic illustrated stops, in two rows if necessary with unmistakable connecting arrows:
1 "Get repository facts" — a small GitHub metadata card labeled "Name · Description · Topics · Language" and an open "README" with highlighted Overview/Features lines.
2 "Build evidence locally" — a paper-selection funnel producing "E0: metadata" and "E1+: README excerpts"; alongside a small comb/highlighter illustrating "RAKE extracts phrases" with two short phrase slips reading "patient intake api" and "orion clinical platform". Metadata is constructed before RAKE. E1 is not a generated purpose statement.
3 "Prepare the request" — an open request booklet with three clearly readable tabs: "System prompt", "Collection JSON", "Output schema". Inside the Collection tab show a few repository rows, not raw JSON prose. A short nearby line says "Each repo: E0 + up to 2 excerpts + up to 8 phrases". This is a bounded collection, not the full README corpus. No canonical shortlist is supplied for discovery.
4 "LLM proposes a draft" — a small friendly model/robot returning a draft page with the four distinct labels "Domain", "Project", "Topic", "Tag". Do not depict all four as one nested chain: Projects have Domain parents, Topics and Tags are independent facets.
5 "Human review" — a person editing/checking the draft with an accepted label card reading "Canonical IDs". Approval comes after generation; the draft is not automatically canonical.
Only one short bottom takeaway: "RAKE finds phrases. The LLM proposes concepts."
Keep total wording limited to the specified short labels. Use source documents and visible transformations, not service boxes. No embeddings, clustering engine, TF-IDF, evaluation metrics, cloud infrastructure, tool-enabled agent loops, private-content upload, API credentials or invented example repository names. Do not use human gold reference labels as model input. No watermark. The graphic should feel spacious, accurate and easy to follow.

Use case: infographic-diagram. Create an original friendly hand-drawn technical explainer, visually consistent with a white-paper sketchbook, dark navy pen, indigo/blue headings, soft light-blue/lavender marker washes, simple semantic objects, readable handwriting and generous whitespace. Landscape target 1920x1080. It accompanies a detailed markdown explanation, so illustrate the main mechanism without printing the full prompts or raw JSON.
Title exactly: "Classifying a repository"
Subtitle: "Retrieve choices locally. Ask the model to choose supported IDs."
CRITICAL MEANING: RAKE phrase extraction and canonical candidate retrieval are PARALLEL uses of locally selected evidence. Do NOT draw RAKE phrases as input to TF-IDF. Do NOT label E1 as guaranteed purpose. Do NOT send all evidence, aliases, scores, private data or human gold answers to the model.
Composition: a clear left-to-right illustrated workspace with three broad, lightly separated regions (no heavy enclosing boxes).
LEFT "Build the evidence": small metadata card ("Name · Description · Topics · Language") and README page flow into an evidence bundle. Label the bundle "E0: metadata" and "E1+: README excerpts".
MIDDLE "Prepare locally": fork the evidence bundle visibly into separate branches.
- Upper branch: "Full selected evidence text" flows to a magnifying glass labeled "TF-IDF + alias boost". A separate nearby approved vocabulary ledger labeled "Canonical registry" feeds this magnifying glass. A small sieve follows, labeled "Filter protected IDs", producing a short stack labeled "Candidate IDs + names + descriptions".
- Lower branch: a small phrase extractor/highlighter labeled "RAKE" produces phrase slips labeled "Up to 8 phrases". Alongside it a small excerpt selector produces "E0 + up to 2 excerpts". Both feed the request, separately from the candidate shortlist.
RIGHT "Send the request": a clear open request booklet receiving the compact excerpts, phrases and candidate slips. Its three readable tabs are "System prompt", "User JSON", "Output schema". A small friendly LLM/robot reads the booklet and returns a paper labeled "IDs + cited evidence". A check/clipboard after it says "Validate → suggestions". No model-created canonical names. A small clean note by the output says "Domains follow Projects".
One bottom takeaway, in readable size: "RAKE supplies phrases. TF-IDF searches evidence text."
Flow arrows must clearly show these distinct input sources and convergence into one bounded request. Minimize decorative filler, avoid tangled crossings, use whitespace to separate the two local branches. No numerical metrics, no confidence charts, no infrastructure, no neural reranker or dense embeddings, no screenshots, no long lists or paragraphs, no tools or private credentials. Keep text large enough for 850px-wide reading. No watermark.
